articles.title: SJAA 2002 fall swap meet
articles.summary: The SJAA is holding its 2002 Fall Swap Meet on Sunday, November 10, 2002, at Houge Park in San Jose, from 1:00 p.m. to approximately 3:00 p.m. This event allows attendees to buy and sell various new and used astronomical equipment, books, space art, and science/tech items, with sellers paying a 10% commission on sales.

articles.title: November speaker Tony Misch
articles.summary: The article announces Tony Misch of Lick Observatory as the November 16th speaker, who will present on the early solar eclipse expeditions of Lick Observatory. His talk, titled "In the Shadow of the Moon," will be largely pictorial, based on recently rediscovered photographic glass plate negatives from these expeditions that occurred from 1889 for over forty years. These expeditions were crucial for studying the sun's corona and left behind invaluable scientific and historical records.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky Saturn spoken here
articles.summary: This article encourages amateur astronomers to observe Saturn in November, detailing key features visible through telescopes due to its high northern hemisphere position. It describes the A, B, and C rings, Cassini's division, and subtle planetary markings, while also challenging observers to look for the 'Encke smudge' and rare radial spokes. A brief mention of other visible planets like Uranus, Neptune, and Jupiter is also included.

articles.title: Leonid Meteor Shower Observing Challenges
articles.summary: The article provides advice for observing the Leonid Meteor Shower under the challenging conditions of a full Moon, suggesting strategies like using a Moon filter and a baseball cap to minimize glare. It also includes an extensive section detailing deep-sky observing targets for November 2002, featuring various galaxies, nebulae, and clusters in constellations such as Cetus, Sculptor, Andromeda, and Cassiopeia, complete with specific observer reports and tips.

articles.title: Deep Sky November
articles.summary: The article introduces Dinosaur Point as a prime dark-sky observing site for south bay amateur astronomers, particularly good between October and March. Access requires special arrangements, often coordinated through TAC's mailing list, and casual visits are discouraged. The site offers amenities like a paved lot, picnic benches, and bathrooms, located at the summit of Pacheco Pass.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar November 2002
articles.summary: This document features a celestial calendar for November 2002, detailing lunar phases, planet positions, and observing conditions. It also reports on the successful Calstar star party organized by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), including suggestions for future improvements. Additionally, it announces a public lecture by Nobel laureate Dr. Arno Penzias on "A Personal View of the Big Bang" scheduled for November 13, 2002, at Foothill College.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article details the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) loaner telescope program, available to all members. It provides lists of telescopes currently available for immediate loan, those currently on loan with their due dates, and scopes with extended loan periods. The document also includes contact information for borrowing a scope and a waiting list for popular equipment.
